Find the smallest n such that n! is divisible by 10^6 (i.e. v_5(n!) >= 6). Output only the integer.
Two steps. Let g = gcd(1071, 462). Then compute a = 1071/g and b = 462/g. Output only all three integers g, a, b (any order, each at least once).
Two steps. Let L = lcm(12, 18). Then compute L^2 mod 100. Output only both integers L and (L^2 mod 100).
Two steps. Let p = phi(81). Then compute 2^p mod 81. Output only both integers p and (2^p mod 81).
Two steps. Let S = 1 + 2 + ... + 19. Then compute S mod 9. Output only both integers S and (S mod 9).
Two counts. A = number of ordered outcomes of two fair dice summing to 9. B = number of ordered outcomes of three fair dice summing to 9. Output only both integers A and B.
Three counts for 1..200. A = multiples of 4. B = multiples of 6. C = multiples of both (i.e. of 12). Output only all three integers A, B, C.
Two steps. First solve x = 2 mod 5 and x = 3 mod 7; let A be the smallest positive solution. Then compute A^2 mod 100 = B. Output only both integers A and B.
Two steps. Let A = 7! Then let B = v_5(A), the exponent of 5 in the prime factorization of A (number of trailing zeros contributed by 5s). Output only both integers A and B.
Two steps. Let A = 3^100 mod 7. Then let B = A^2 mod 7. Output only both integers A and B.
Two steps. Let A = 2^20. Let B = the sum of the decimal digits of A. Output only both integers A and B.
